title: Her Rutgers workshop diploma and the Tony nomination
summary: A 1960 community leadership workshop certificate and a Tony nomination for 'My Old Friends'; she's working harder now.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Look at this, you see Maxine is actually an alumnae of Rutgers University. That was 1960. Here's her diploma.
What does it say? She attended the workshop?

"Workshop, community leadership and inter-group relations conducted as part of the summer session of the University, by the School of Education, Rutgers, the State University, New Brunswick, New Jersey, July 23rd, 1960."
You got that in Newark. How did you get over to New Brunswick?

Nutley, Nutley, we stayed at Demarest Hall. We were out there for a week.

Nomination Antoinette Perry award. "Outstanding performance by a featured actress in a musical. Maxine Sullivan, My Old Friends, 1978 and '79. League of New York Theaters and Producers, Inc. Presented under the authorization of the American Theater Wing, Inc." That's beautiful. If you don't you should feel very proud of yourself.
Oh, yes, you're doing more than hanging in there.
You had a Tony nomination for that.
I'm working harder now than I did when I was young.
I think I saw that on television.
